subject: FinTechCo: Pricing follow-up - US vs EU residency & $/1M token estimate
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@fintechco.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: FinTechCo - pricing follow-up (US vs EU residency / $/1M token target)

Hi Alice / Raj  great meeting this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps from our side:  

- Current ask: validate cost envelope for a pilot and a 12-month forecast given your expected token volumes and residency needs.  
- FinTechCo estimated query volumes: 500M input tokens / month, 2.5B output tokens / month (burst to 4B). Total ~3B tokens/month. Please flag if these are off.  
- Budget guidance you mentioned on the call: target cost of ~$2,500 - $5,000 / 1M tokens (company-wide blended target)  we explored how that maps to model choices and region.  

Notes on regional impact (high level):  
- US vs EU unit-cost delta: EU-anchored deployments typically add ~10-25% to unit costs due to data residency overhead, cross-region storage, and multiregion HA requirements. Precise delta depends on model variant, committed capacity, and whether you opt for our Dedicated pools in eu-west vs hosted in the US.  
- Data residency: if traffic and KV-caches need to stay in EU, we serve from eu regions and apply the EU rate card. If you want to keep control plane in US but data in EU, there are hybrid options but that increases complexity and some costs.  

Next steps (proposed):  
1) We'll send a concise pricing estimate with US vs EU unit price at three commitment tiers (pilot, mid, enterprise).  
2) You confirm final expected monthly tokens and whether all tokens must be EU-resident.  
3) If the range looks good, we'll draft an SOW + committed capacity options and loop procurement.  

Attachments I will send: redwood_pricing_estimate_fintechco_us_eu.xlsx (breakdowns), SOW_draft_v1.pdf (placeholder).  

Deliverable timeline: draft estimate by EOD today (sending now), SOW draft within 48 hours after we confirm volumes.  

Thanks  happy to jump on another quick call if you want to walk the numbers.  

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@fintechco.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinTechCo - pricing follow-up (US vs EU residency / $/1M token target)

Thanks Dylan  helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side:  

- The 3B tokens/month is the high-end forecast (post-product launch). For the pilot (Q1) we expect ~200M total/month.  
- Critical: for regulatory reasons, token-level data for EU customers must remain within the EU. That applies to both input and output (no cross-border replication).  
- Our target blended $/1M tokens is closer to $3,000 for year 1; we might be able to increase that for year 2 if we get to the higher volumes you showed.  

Can you confirm: if we require full EU residency for EU traffic, what's the expected unit price difference vs serving from US? Also, what commit levels drive the biggest per-token discounts?

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

 Alice
Head of Platform
FinTechCo

---

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@fintechco.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinTechCo - pricing follow-up (US vs EU residency / $/1M token target)

Alice  thanks for the clarifications, and understood re: EU-only residency for EU customer traffic. Below is a concise estimate and the assumptions I used. I'll attach the detailed spreadsheet.  

Assumptions (short):  
- Model: mix of an open LLM quantized for throughput (blended across generations)  we'll propose a primary model + fallback smaller model for low-latency flows.  
- Pilot (200M tokens/mo), Mid (1B tokens/mo), Target (3B tokens/mo).  
- Pricing baseline: Hosted US region base unit = $3,200 / 1M tokens (blended for generation + prompt tokens) w/out commit.  
- EU residency uplift: +15% on unit price for EU-hosted serving with HA and EU KV/cache retention (this includes higher infra FOB and cross-region replication avoidance).  
- Committed discounts: 20% at 1B/month commit, 35% at 3B/month commit (applied to base before region uplift).  

Estimated unit economics (rounded):  
- Pilot (200M/mo): US hosted (no commit): $3,200 / 1M => pilot monthly cost = $640k. EU hosted: $3,200 *1.15 = $3,680 / 1M => pilot = $736k.  
- Mid (1B/mo, 20% commit): US: $3,200 *0.8 = $2,560 / 1M => monthly = $2.56M. EU: $2,560 *1.15 = $2,944 / 1M => monthly = $2.944M.  
- Target (3B/mo, 35% commit): US: $3,200 *0.65 = $2,080 / 1M => monthly = $6.24M. EU: $2,080 *1.15 = $2,392 / 1M => monthly = $7.176M.  

Observations:  
- Your blended target of ~$3,000 / 1M is reachable at the mid tier if you commit to ~1B/month (US-hosted net $2,560 / 1M and EU-hosted $2,944 / 1M).  
- If you need EU residency for all EU traffic, we can structure routing so EU tokens are served from eu-west and US tokens from us-west to avoid cross-border storage; the blended company-wide rate will depend on customer geography mix.  
- Additional savings levers: dedicated reserved pools (further 5-10% depending on term), aggressive KV/cache sharing within residency constraints, and model quantization choices (can reduce cost by ~10-20% vs baseline).  

Next steps:  
- I attached the detailed workbook (redwood_pricing_estimate_fintechco_us_eu.xlsx) with line-by-line math.  
- Please confirm: (1) % of customer tokens that are EU-resident (ballpark 0-100%), (2) whether you want us to price committed reserved capacity (12/24 month) vs purely hosted.  

If that looks good, Marissa and I will draft an SOW and include committed capacity options for procurement to review. Happy to hop on a call to walk the spreadsheet.  

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_pricing_estimate_fintechco_us_eu.xlsx (pricing workbook)

- Alice: we'll include an enterprise SOW draft today that includes the reserved capacity option and explicit EU-hosted routing.
